CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pesawaran Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of government which is the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pesawaran. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Pesawaran Regency. 5. Sub-district is a part of the Regency area led by a sub-district head. 6. Village is a part of the Regency area led by a Village Head; 7. Village Government is the village government in Pesawaran Regency. 8. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children or mother and her children or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward laterally to the third degree. 10. Parents are biological father and/or mother or step father and/or step mother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 11. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises custody as a parent over a child. 12. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. 13. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a baby still in the womb. 14. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 16. Protection of women is any effort made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 17. Empowerment of women is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 18. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 19. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 20. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 21. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the Child into the environment of the adoptive Parents' Family based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. 23. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the Child in accordance with the religion professed and in accordance with the ability, talent, and interest. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field. 26. Violence is any act unlawfully, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom. 27. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 28. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 29. Child-Friendly Regency is a Regency that has a Development and Public Service system from the Regency Government with support from parents, families, communities, private sector and Children's Forum for the fulfillment of children's rights through the integration of commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably through policies, programs, activities and budgeting for the welfare of children. 30. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a cooperative network that organizes integrated social service functions. 31. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that organizes integrated service functions for the protection of women and children. 32. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations. 33. Family Welfare Consultation Institution hereinafter abbreviated as LK3 is an integrated social service unit that implements psychosocial problem handling for families to realize family resilience. 34. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an integrated social service unit that implements child protection services to realize the fulfillment of children's rights. 35.

Article 69

1. The obligations and responsibilities of parents and family as referred to in Article 45 letter d, are to safeguard and prevent the occurrence of all forms of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination both against women and against children.
2. The obligations and responsibilities of parents towards children as referred to in paragraph (1), are to:
a. care for, maintain, educate, and protect children;
b. develop children according to their abilities, talents, and interests;
c. prevent the occurrence of marriage at child age; and
d. provide character education and instillation of moral values in children.
3. Guardians and/or foster parents appointed as referred to in paragraph (3) must have the same religion as that professed by the Child.
4. Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be responsible for the child and must manage the property of the child concerned for the best interests of the child.
5. Guardians and/or foster parents as referred to in paragraph (3), may represent the child to perform legal acts, both inside and outside the court for the best interests of the child.

Article 46

1. Protection in the education field as referred to in Article 37 letter c applies within and in the environment of education units.
2. Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of protection from acts of physical violence, psychological violence, sexual crimes, and other crimes.
3. Protection within and outside education units may be carried out by educators, education personnel, regional government officials, and/or the community.

Article 66

1. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 65 letter a, the Regent shall establish programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.
2. The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
3. Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Four

Protection of Women

Article 17

Every child has the right to live, grow, develop, and participate reasonably in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from violence and discrimination.

Article 30

1. Every child who is deprived of his/her freedom has the right to:
a. receive humane treatment and placement separated from adults;
b. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
c. defend himself/herself and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed session to the public.
2. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.

Article 22

1. Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing his/her personality and level of intelligence in accordance with his/her interests and talents.
2. Every Child has the right to receive protection in educational units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
3. In addition to obtaining Children's Rights as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), Children with Disabilities have the right to obtain special education and Children who have excellence have the right to receive special education.

Article 60

Special Protection for Child victims of maltreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 49 letter l is carried out through efforts of supervision, prevention, care, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance.

Article 71

1. P2TP2A as referred to in Article 70 paragraph (3) letter a, shall be positioned at the regional level and sub-district level.
2. P2TP2A shall be under the coordination of OPD or other units that handle women's empowerment and child protection.
3. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) does not have the authority to formulate policies on women's empowerment and child protection.
4. P2TP2A is one form of integrated service unit, which functions as:
a. an information center for women and children;
b. a service center for women and children victims of violence; and
c. an empowerment center for women and children.

3. Further provisions regarding P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

1. The Regional Government shall facilitate the establishment of a children's forum.
2. The children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes a representation of children in Pesawaran Regency, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational background.

CHAPTER VII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Part One

Article 70

1. In the context of protection of women and children, the Regional Government may establish PPT.
2. The establishment and development of PPT shall be adjusted to priority needs, regional financial capacity as well as institutional and personnel capacity available in the region.
3. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), may take the form of:
a. P2TP2A;
b. LK3;
c. KPAD; and
d. other institutions according to needs and in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 73

1. In the context of handling psychosocial problems of victims, recovery of psychosocial conditions of victims and strengthening family resilience, LK3 may be established in the region.
2. The procedures for establishment, main duties and functions as well as service mechanisms of LK3 shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 39

1. Parents and families provide protection to maintain children's health starting from examination of the child's developmental growth from the womb.
2. In the event that parents and families are unable to carry out protection as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government is obliged to fulfill it.
3. The Regional Government provides free assistance and services for communities who are unable to afford them as referred to in paragraph (2), and its implementation is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 71

1. P2TP2A as referred to in Article 70 paragraph (3) letter a, shall be positioned at the regional level and sub-district level.
2. P2TP2A shall be under the coordination of OPD or other units that handle women's empowerment and child protection.
3. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) does not have the authority to formulate policies on women's empowerment and child protection.
4. P2TP2A is one form of integrated service unit, which functions as:
a. an information center for women and children;
b. a service center for women and children victims of violence; and
c. an empowerment center for women and children.

Article 82

1. To assist the smooth implementation of the duties of the Child-Friendly Regency Task Force, a Secretariat is established.
2. The Secretariat as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing technical and administrative support to the Child-Friendly Regency Task Force.
3. The Secretariat of the Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is located at the Office of the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Agency.
4. The establishment of the secretariat and appointment of secretariat personnel of the Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is determined by the Regional Head.

CHAPTER X

Article 83

1. The special development planning forum for women and children is a form of annual meeting or gathering held specifically for women and children to explore various ideas and inputs for the fulfillment of women's and children's rights in regional development programs and activities.
2. The special development planning forum for women and children is implemented before the implementation of the development planning forum.
3. Further provisions regarding the implementation mechanism of the special development planning forum for women and children as referred to in paragraph (1), are regulated by Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL

That human beings are endowed by God Almighty with reason and conscience which gives them the ability to distinguish between good and bad which will guide and direct attitudes and behavior in living their lives. With their reason and conscience, humans have the freedom to decide for themselves their behavior or actions. In addition, to balance that freedom, humans have the ability to be responsible for all actions they take.

Those basic freedoms and basic rights are what are called human rights which are inherently attached to humans naturally as a gift from God Almighty. These rights cannot be denied. Denial of these rights means denying human dignity. Therefore, the state, government, or any organization bears the obligation to recognize and protect human rights for every human being without exception. This means that human rights must always be the starting point and goal in the administration of social, national and state life.

The State upholds human rights, including Children's rights, which is marked by the guarantee of protection and fulfillment of Children's Rights in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and several provisions of laws and regulations both national and international in nature. This guarantee is strengthened through the ratification of international conventions on Children's Rights, namely the ratification of the Convention on the Rights of the Child through Presidential Decree Number 36 of 1990 concerning Ratification of the Convention On The Rights Of The Child.

The State, Government, Regional Government, Community, Family and Parents are obliged to provide protection and ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights in accordance with their duties and responsibilities. Protection of Children that has been carried out so far has not provided guarantees for Children to receive treatment and opportunities in accordance with their needs in various areas of life, so that in implementing efforts to protect Children's Rights, the Government must be based on the principles of human rights, namely respect, fulfillment, and protection of Children's Rights.

I. GENERAL

That human beings are endowed by God Almighty with reason and conscience which gives them the ability to distinguish between good and bad which will guide and direct attitudes and behavior in living their lives. With their reason and conscience, humans have the freedom to decide for themselves their behavior or actions. In addition, to balance that freedom, humans have the ability to be responsible for all actions they take.

Those basic freedoms and basic rights are what are called human rights which are inherently attached to humans naturally as a gift from God Almighty. These rights cannot be denied. Denial of these rights means denying human dignity. Therefore, the state, government, or any organization bears the obligation to recognize and protect human rights for every human being without exception. This means that human rights must always be the starting point and goal in the administration of social, national and state life.

The State upholds human rights, including Children's rights, which is marked by the guarantee of protection and fulfillment of Children's Rights in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and several provisions of laws and regulations both national and international in nature. This guarantee is strengthened through the ratification of international conventions on Children's Rights, namely the ratification of the Convention on the Rights of the Child through Presidential Decree Number 36 of 1990 concerning Ratification of the Convention On The Rights Of The Child.

The State, Government, Regional Government, Community, Family and Parents are obliged to provide protection and ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights in accordance with their duties and responsibilities. Protection of Children that has been carried out so far has not provided guarantees for Children to receive treatment and opportunities in accordance with their needs in various areas of life, so that in implementing efforts to protect Children's Rights, the Government must be based on the principles of human rights, namely respect, fulfillment, and protection of Children's Rights.

I. GENERAL

That human beings are endowed by God Almighty with reason and conscience which gives them the ability to distinguish between good and bad which will guide and direct attitudes and behavior in living their lives. With their reason and conscience, humans have the freedom to decide for themselves their behavior or actions. In addition, to balance that freedom, humans have the ability to be responsible for all actions they take.

Those basic freedoms and basic rights are what are called human rights which are inherently attached to humans naturally as a gift from God Almighty. These rights cannot be denied. Denial of these rights means denying human dignity. Therefore, the state, government, or any organization bears the obligation to recognize and protect human rights for every human being without exception. This means that human rights must always be the starting point and goal in the administration of social, national and state life.

The State upholds human rights, including Children's rights, which is marked by the guarantee of protection and fulfillment of Children's Rights in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and several provisions of laws and regulations both national and international in nature. This guarantee is strengthened through the ratification of international conventions on Children's Rights, namely the ratification of the Convention on the Rights of the Child through Presidential Decree Number 36 of 1990 concerning Ratification of the Convention On The Rights Of The Child.

The State, Government, Regional Government, Community, Family and Parents are obliged to provide protection and ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights in accordance with their duties and responsibilities. Protection of Children that has been carried out so far has not provided guarantees for Children to receive treatment and opportunities in accordance with their needs in various areas of life, so that in implementing efforts to protect Children's Rights, the Government must be based on the principles of human rights, namely respect, fulfillment, and protection of Children's Rights.

2. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.

Article 31

Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act has the right to receive legal assistance and other assistance.

I. GENERAL

That human beings are endowed by God Almighty with reason and conscience which gives them the ability to distinguish between good and bad which will guide and direct attitudes and behavior in living their lives. With their reason and conscience, humans have the freedom to decide for themselves their behavior or actions. In addition, to balance that freedom, humans have the ability to be responsible for all actions they take.

Those basic freedoms and basic rights are what are called human rights which are inherently attached to humans naturally as a gift from God Almighty. These rights cannot be denied. Denial of these rights means denying human dignity. Therefore, the state, government, or any organization bears the obligation to recognize and protect human rights for every human being without exception. This means that human rights must always be the starting point and goal in the administration of social, national and state life.

The State upholds human rights, including Children's rights, which is marked by the guarantee of protection and fulfillment of Children's Rights in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and several provisions of laws and regulations both national and international in nature. This guarantee is strengthened through the ratification of international conventions on Children's Rights, namely the ratification of the Convention on the Rights of the Child through Presidential Decree Number 36 of 1990 concerning Ratification of the Convention On The Rights Of The Child.

The State, Government, Regional Government, Community, Family and Parents are obliged to provide protection and ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights in accordance with their duties and responsibilities. Protection of Children that has been carried out so far has not provided guarantees for Children to receive treatment and opportunities in accordance with their needs in various areas of life, so that in implementing efforts to protect Children's Rights, the Government must be based on the principles of human rights, namely respect, fulfillment, and protection of Children's Rights.

Article 39

1. Parents and families provide protection to maintain children's health starting from examination of the child's developmental growth from the womb.
2. In the event that parents and families are unable to carry out protection as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government is obliged to fulfill it.
3. The Regional Government provides free assistance and services for communities who are unable to afford them as referred to in paragraph (2), and its implementation is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 15

a. families;
b. the community; and
c. women's advocacy institutions.

Article 48

1. Child protection in the Social field as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) letter d, includes maintenance and care of neglected children.
2. Maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. fulfillment of basic needs consisting of clothing, food, shelter, education, health, security guarantees, freedom to worship according to their religion and equal treatment with other children to achieve social integration as optimally as possible; and
b. fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities.
3. Maintenance of neglected children as referred to in paragraph (1), may also be carried out by individuals and non-governmental institutions or community institutions.
4. Regional government institutions, and/or individuals, and/or community institutions in providing services as referred to in paragraph (2), may cooperate with various related service units.
5. Supervision of the implementation of maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out by regional apparatus organizations (OPD) that administer affairs in the social field in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 75

1. The Regional Government shall facilitate the establishment of a children's forum.
2. The children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes a representation of children in Pesawaran Regency, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational background.
3. In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of children conveyed through the children's forum.
4. The establishment of the children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regional Head Decree.
5. Sources of financing for the implementation of children's forum activities may come from:
a. contributions from members of the children's forum;
b. donations from the community/private parties that are non-binding in nature;
c. assistance from the Regional Government; and/ord. other sources of financing in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 29

1. Every child has the right to obtain protection from being the target of persecution, torture, or imposition of inhuman punishment.
2. Every child has the right to obtain freedom in accordance with the law.
3. Arrest, detention, or criminal imprisonment of a child shall only be carried out if in accordance with applicable law and can only be carried out as a last resort.

Article 60

Special Protection for Child victims of maltreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 49 letter l is carried out through efforts of supervision, prevention, care, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance.

Article 30

1. Every child who is deprived of his/her freedom has the right to:
a. receive humane treatment and placement separated from adults;
b. obtain legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
c. defend himself/herself and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed session to the public.
2. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.

Article 31

Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act has the right to receive legal assistance and other assistance.

I. GENERAL

That human beings are endowed by God Almighty with reason and conscience which gives them the ability to distinguish between good and bad which will guide and direct attitudes and behavior in living their lives. With their reason and conscience, humans have the freedom to decide for themselves their behavior or actions. In addition, to balance that freedom, humans have the ability to be responsible for all actions they take.

Those basic freedoms and basic rights are what are called human rights which are inherently attached to humans naturally as a gift from God Almighty. These rights cannot be denied. Denial of these rights means denying human dignity. Therefore, the state, government, or any organization bears the obligation to recognize and protect human rights for every human being without exception. This means that human rights must always be the starting point and goal in the administration of social, national and state life.

The State upholds human rights, including Children's rights, which is marked by the guarantee of protection and fulfillment of Children's Rights in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and several provisions of laws and regulations both national and international in nature. This guarantee is strengthened through the ratification of international conventions on Children's Rights, namely the ratification of the Convention on the Rights of the Child through Presidential Decree Number 36 of 1990 concerning Ratification of the Convention On The Rights Of The Child.

The State, Government, Regional Government, Community, Family and Parents are obliged to provide protection and ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights in accordance with their duties and responsibilities. Protection of Children that has been carried out so far has not provided guarantees for Children to receive treatment and opportunities in accordance with their needs in various areas of life, so that in implementing efforts to protect Children's Rights, the Government must be based on the principles of human rights, namely respect, fulfillment, and protection of Children's Rights.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESAWARAN REGENCY

NUMBER 1 OF 2019 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

That human beings are endowed by God Almighty with reason and conscience which gives them the ability to distinguish between good and bad which will guide and direct attitudes and behavior in living their lives. With their reason and conscience, humans have the freedom to decide for themselves their behavior or actions. In addition, to balance that freedom, humans have the ability to be responsible for all actions they take.

Those basic freedoms and basic rights are what are called human rights which are inherently attached to humans naturally as a gift from God Almighty. These rights cannot be denied. Denial of these rights means denying human dignity. Therefore, the state, government, or any organization bears the obligation to recognize and protect human rights for every human being without exception. This means that human rights must always be the starting point and goal in the administration of social, national and state life.

The State upholds human rights, including Children's rights, which is marked by the guarantee of protection and fulfillment of Children's Rights in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and several provisions of laws and regulations both national and international in nature. This guarantee is strengthened through the ratification of international conventions on Children's Rights, namely the ratification of the Convention on the Rights of the Child through Presidential Decree Number 36 of 1990 concerning Ratification of the Convention On The Rights Of The Child.

The State, Government, Regional Government, Community, Family and Parents are obliged to provide protection and ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights in accordance with their duties and responsibilities. Protection of Children that has been carried out so far has not provided guarantees for Children to receive treatment and opportunities in accordance with their needs in various areas of life, so that in implementing efforts to protect Children's Rights, the Government must be based on the principles of human rights, namely respect, fulfillment, and protection of Children's Rights.

I. GENERAL

That human beings are endowed by God Almighty with reason and conscience which gives them the ability to distinguish between good and bad which will guide and direct attitudes and behavior in living their lives. With their reason and conscience, humans have the freedom to decide for themselves their behavior or actions. In addition, to balance that freedom, humans have the ability to be responsible for all actions they take.

Denial of these rights means denying human dignity. Therefore, the state, government, or any organization bears the obligation to recognize and protect human rights for every human being without exception. This means that human rights must always be the starting point and goal in the administration of social, national and state life.

This guarantee is strengthened through the ratification of international conventions on Children's Rights, namely the ratification of the Convention on the Rights of the Child through Presidential Decree Number 36 of 1990 concerning Ratification of the Convention On The Rights Of The Child.

The State, Government, Regional Government, Community, Family and Parents are obliged to provide protection and ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights in accordance with their duties and responsibilities. Protection of Children that has been carried out so far has not provided guarantees for Children to receive treatment and opportunities in accordance with their needs in various areas of life, so that in implementing efforts to protect Children's Rights, the Government must be based on the principles of human rights, namely respect, fulfillment, and protection of Children's Rights.

a. economic;
b. socio-cultural;
c. political; and
d. legal.

Children's Forum is a Social Organization that represents the voice and participation of children that is independent and not affiliated with political organizations where the establishment and preparation of its activities are determined in the Regent's Regulation. 36. Gender mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies. 37. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 38. Safe House (Shelter) is a shelter for women and children including families and witnesses of victims of violence.

Article 38

1. Protection in the health field as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) letter a, is carried out by the government through the provision of health facilities and efforts to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains the optimal degree of health from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.
3. Comprehensive health service efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented by the Regional Government free of charge for families who are unable to afford them.

Article 40

1. Every Child has the right to be cared for by his/her own Parents, unless there are valid legal reasons and/or rules showing that the separation is in the best interests of the Child and is a last consideration.
2. In the event of separation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Child still has the right to:
a. meet directly and maintain personal relations regularly with both Parents;
b. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both Parents in accordance with abilities, talents, and interests;
c. obtain living expenses from both Parents; and
d. obtain other Children's Rights."

CHAPTER XI

FINANCING

Article 84

The costs of implementing the protection of women and children are sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. Other legitimate and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 75

1. The Regional Government shall facilitate the establishment of a children's forum.
2. The children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes a representation of children in Pesawaran Regency, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational background.
3. In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of children conveyed through the children's forum.
4. The establishment of the children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regional Head Decree.
5. Sources of financing for the implementation of children's forum activities may come from:
a. contributions from members of the children's forum;
b. donations from the community/private parties that are non-binding in nature;
c. assistance from the Regional Government; and/ord. other sources of financing in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Part Two

Regional Government

CHAPTER VII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Part One

Article 70

1. In the context of protection of women and children, the Regional Government may establish PPT.
2. The establishment and development of PPT shall be adjusted to priority needs, regional financial capacity as well as institutional and personnel capacity available in the region.
3. PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), may take the form of:
a. P2TP2A;
b. LK3;
c. KPAD; and
d. other institutions according to needs and in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 39

1. Parents and families provide protection to maintain children's health starting from examination of the child's developmental growth from the womb.
2. In the event that parents and families are unable to carry out protection as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government is obliged to fulfill it.
3. The Regional Government provides free assistance and services for communities who are unable to afford them as referred to in paragraph (2), and its implementation is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pesawaran Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of government which is the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pesawaran. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Pesawaran Regency. 5. Sub-district is a part of the Regency area led by a sub-district head. 6. Village is a part of the Regency area led by a Village Head; 7. Village Government is the village government in Pesawaran Regency. 8. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 9. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children or mother and her children or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward laterally to the third degree. 10. Parents are biological father and/or mother or step father and/or step mother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 11. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises custody as a parent over a child. 12. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. 13. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a baby still in the womb. 14. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 16. Protection of women is any effort made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 17. Empowerment of women is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 18. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 19. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 20. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 21. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the Child into the environment of the adoptive Parents' Family based on a court decision or determination. 22. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. 23. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the Child in accordance with the religion professed and in accordance with the ability, talent, and interest. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field. 26. Violence is any act unlawfully, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom. 27. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 28. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 29. Child-Friendly Regency is a Regency that has a Development and Public Service system from the Regency Government with support from parents, families, communities, private sector and Children's Forum for the fulfillment of children's rights through the integration of commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably through policies, programs, activities and budgeting for the welfare of children. 30. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a cooperative network that organizes integrated social service functions. 31. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that organizes integrated service functions for the protection of women and children. 32. Community Social Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and/or other community organizations. 33. Family Welfare Consultation Institution hereinafter abbreviated as LK3 is an integrated social service unit that implements psychosocial problem handling for families to realize family resilience. 34. Regional Child Protection Commission hereinafter abbreviated as KPAD is an integrated social service unit that implements child protection services to realize the fulfillment of children's rights. 35.

Article 38

1. Protection in the health field as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) letter a, is carried out by the government through the provision of health facilities and efforts to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains the optimal degree of health from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals.
3. Comprehensive health service efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented by the Regional Government free of charge for families who are unable to afford them.

Article 47

Special services as referred to in Article 33, in addition to assistance in the form of money, school equipment, may also be in the form of provision of school shuttle buses, the procurement of which is in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Article 45

The Regional Government provides education costs and/or free assistance or special services for children from families who are unable to afford them, neglected children, and children in remote areas.

Article 66

1. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 65 letter a, the Regent shall establish programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing the protection of women and children from acts of violence, exploitation, trafficking and discrimination.
2. The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
3. Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VI

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Part One

General

Article 48

1. Child protection in the Social field as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) letter d, includes maintenance and care of neglected children.
2. Maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. fulfillment of basic needs consisting of clothing, food, shelter, education, health, security guarantees, freedom to worship according to their religion and equal treatment with other children to achieve social integration as optimally as possible; and
b. fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities.
3. Maintenance of neglected children as referred to in paragraph (1), may also be carried out by individuals and non-governmental institutions or community institutions.
4. Regional government institutions, and/or individuals, and/or community institutions in providing services as referred to in paragraph (2), may cooperate with various related service units.
5. Supervision of the implementation of maintenance and care as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out by regional apparatus organizations (OPD) that administer affairs in the social field in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 42

1. Every child receives protection in the education field as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) letter c, to obtain education.
2. The Regional Government, parents, and families must provide the widest possible opportunity for children to obtain education from an early age.
3. The Regional Government provides adequate facilities and infrastructure to support the teaching and learning process for children.
4. Non-governmental institutions may provide teaching and learning facilities and infrastructure for children, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 78

1. The physical condition of an area in which there are facilities and infrastructure managed in such a way as to meet the minimum requirements for the healthy and normal growth and development of children, not containing elements that endanger children.
2. Suitability as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of infrastructure such as highways, bridges, sidewalks, transportation facilities, regency parks, green living environment and the availability of supporting legal instruments.
3. Suitability as referred to in paragraph (2) is implemented at the village, sub-district and Regency levels as well as in the provision of public services, including in the education and health sectors.

Part Four

Community

Article 44

1. The Regional Government provides protection for children with disabilities, to obtain opportunities and accessibility to obtain inclusive education and/or special education.
2. Children who have excellence are given the opportunity to obtain special education.

Article 12

1. The Regional Government is obliged and responsible in efforts to empower women.
2. Efforts to empower women as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Part Three

Village Government

Article 71

1. P2TP2A as referred to in Article 70 paragraph (3) letter a, shall be positioned at the regional level and sub-district level.
2. P2TP2A shall be under the coordination of OPD or other units that handle women's empowerment and child protection.
3. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) does not have the authority to formulate policies on women's empowerment and child protection.
4. P2TP2A is one form of integrated service unit, which functions as:
a. an information center for women and children;
b. a service center for women and children victims of violence; and
c. an empowerment center for women and children.
